question: The most frequent mechanism that induces the activation of the BCL2 protooncogene in follicular lymphoma is:
analysis: Follicular lymphoma is commonly associated with a specific chromosomal translocation, most notably t(14;18), which results in the juxtaposition of the BCL2 gene with the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus. This translocation leads to the overexpression of the BCL2 protein, inhibiting apoptosis and contributing to the survival of malignant B cells. Therefore, the most frequent mechanism that induces the activation of the BCL2 protooncogene in follicular lymphoma is translocation.
